# The engine's default reveal chrome vanishes on a dark ground

Sub-issue of #13158 (dock layouts). Seen on 2026-09-02 while reading #18074's reveal motion on the served `dock-popout` fixture in the neo-dark theme; filed on the operator's word so it does not get lost.

## Context

A revealed auto-hidden pane is an overlay over the workspace. The engine paints it from four theme-agnostic tokens (`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss:128-133`): `--dock-reveal-background: var(--neo-background-color, #fff)`, `--dock-reveal-border: 0`, `--dock-reveal-radius: 0`, `--dock-reveal-shadow: 0 12px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 28%)`. The comment above them says why: "A reveal is an overlay, so opacity and elevation are functional rather than decorative" — the shadow IS the edge.

## The Problem

On a dark ground the shadow is not an edge. In neo-dark the overlay's background resolves to the same surface color as the pane beneath it (`--neo-background-color` → `--sem-color-bg-neutral-default`), the border is `0`, and a 28%-black shadow on a near-black ground is invisible — the revealed pane reads as the pane it covers, with a title line floating in it. Read on the fixture: the settled overlay over `Pinned` is indistinguishable from `Pinned` except for its header text.

Both flagship hosts already override the tokens because of this: `apps/workstation` (`resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss:98-104` — its rail surface, a 1px signal-mixed border, an 8px radius, a 72%-ground shadow plus a signal glow; measured live: background `rgb(14 19 26)` beside a cell at `rgb(20 26 35)`, border `1px solid` teal) and the Fleet cockpit (`neo-agent-institution` `fleet/cockpit/Container.scss:182-185` — `--fm-rail` background, `1px solid var(--fm-line)` border). Every other consumer — the dock example, the component fixtures, a new adopter, a client workspace that has not written those lines — gets the invisible default. The engine's job is a discoverable overlay by default; aesthetics are the consumer's (the splitter-affordance floor in the same file states the same principle, `:22-31`).

## The Architectural Reality

- The reveal tokens are declared once on `.neo-dashboard` in `Container.scss` and are theme-agnostic; no theme file sets them (`grep -rn dock-reveal resources/scss` finds only the two app overrides). The neo themes' surface vocabulary lives in `theme-neo-dark/Global.scss` / `theme-neo-light/Global.scss` (`--neo-background-color`, the `--sem-color-*` set).
- The splitter floor (`:22-31`) shows the house pattern for a discoverability floor: values resolve through `currentColor` so the engine needs no knowledge of the host palette; a `color-mix` band reads on any ground.
- #14779 owns motion; this is paint. #18070 (landed as PR #18073) owns where the overlay starts; this is what its edge looks like once it is there.

## The Fix

A discoverability floor for the reveal's edge that reads on any ground, in the engine defaults — the same `currentColor` pattern as the splitter floor:

1. `--dock-reveal-border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 22%, transparent)` — a hairline that separates the overlay from an identical surface beneath it, light or dark, without naming a color.
2. `--dock-reveal-shadow`: keep the elevation, make it read on dark: a two-layer shadow — the existing soft drop plus a wide low-alpha `currentColor` halo (`0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 8%, transparent)` or a `color-mix` glow) so elevation survives a black ground.
3. No radius change (consumers set it), no background change (the surface stays the host's).
4. A paint witness in the component tier (the `DockRailTabPaint` pattern: measured computed values on the mounted overlay in BOTH neo themes): the overlay's computed border is not `0px none` and its box-shadow is not `none`; plus a luminance-delta read at the overlay's edge against the pane beneath, honest in either skin (the AgentCard witness's contrast guard is the precedent).
5. The two app overrides stay as they are (they are stronger than the floor and win on specificity).

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dock-reveal-border` default (`Container.scss:129`) | this ticket | `1px solid color-mix(currentColor 22%)` | consumer override wins | token comment | paint arm, both themes |
| `--dock-reveal-shadow` default (`:133`) | this ticket | drop + `currentColor` halo | same | same | same |
| `apps/workstation`, Fleet cockpit overrides | existing | unchanged | — | — | their e2e reveal witnesses unchanged |

Decision Record impact: none (ADR 0029 §2.7 describes the reveal as an overlay; paint is a theme floor).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On the `dock-popout` fixture in neo-dark AND neo-light, the mounted overlay's computed border is a visible hairline and its box-shadow is not `none`; a luminance delta at the overlay's edge against the pane beneath exceeds a stated floor in both skins. Red on `dev` in neo-dark (border `0px`, delta ≈ 0).
- [ ] `apps/workstation` and the dock example render byte-identically where they override; where they do not, the floor shows (screenshots, design-read).
- [ ] `check-scss`/lint green; no consumer SCSS change needed.

## Out of Scope

- The reveal's motion (#18074 / PR #18079), its start geometry (#18070), its radius and surface color (consumer decisions).
